items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: there I met Bruce and the boys, Ray Crance, trumpet, Pete Strange, trombone, Tony Baylis, bass, Ron Ruben, piano, and Doug Higgins, drums

ctx.x: I arrived in London with Lily the 6th of April and learned that the tour would be made with the Bruce Turner orchestra. I knew of Bruce but had never met him. He had the reputation of being one of England's greatest alto sax players, and as the tour continued, I found this to be true. But first I must say that Lily and I liked the looks of everything from the moment we landed at Heathrow airport. And we became more and more excited as we approached the great city of London. A kitchenette apartment had been…

That afternoon we had a rehearsal at the Six Bells in Chealsea, which is a district of London. The Six Bells was a very well known place by musicians and jazz fans and there I met Bruce and the boys, Ray Crance, trumpet, Pete Strange, trombone, Tony Baylis, bass, Ron Ruben, piano, and Doug Higgins, drums, Jack Higgins, not related to Doug, was in charge of the jazz department at the Harold Davison Agency, but Jim Godbolt was going to take care of the band during the tour.

We had a second rehearsal the 7th and pkayed our first concert at Osterley which was the town where most of the American musicians that were booked by the Davison agency started their tour of England. Most of those musicians were accompanied by the Alex Welch orchestra which is one of England's best jazz groups. Why Bruce Turner was chosen for me, I never knew. But I can say, and very happily, that I enjoyed every moment that I spent with Bruce Turner and his boys.
